stories.summary: The U.S. has no national law for paid parental leave. But in states that do, more dads are using the benefit, sometimes more than moms. The change comes as Americans say having kids is unaffordable.

stories.title: Popular cannabis sleep gummies may have a hidden dark side
stories.summary: A cannabis-derived ingredient commonly found in sleep gummies may be more habit-forming than previously thought, with new research showing that repeated exposure caused tolerance and withdrawal symptoms in mice.

stories.title: Scientists reveal the hidden danger of missing blood pressure medication
stories.summary: Missing blood pressure medication could mean losing much of its protection against heart attacks and strokes, according to an analysis of more than 91,000 people.

stories.title: The debating club that helped shape NHS architect Aneurin Bevan's drive for power
stories.summary: How a group of young radicals helped set Aneurin Bevan on the path to founding the NHS.

stories.title: U.S. measles cases more than double what they were last year as outbreak spreads
stories.summary: Pennsylvania is the worst hit state, with at least 1,338 cases of measles confirmed in 44 counties so far this year, according to the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

stories.title: Could lowering high blood pressure be as simple as stimulating your ear?
stories.summary: A small device that gently stimulates nerves through the ear could offer a new way to tackle stubborn high blood pressure. In a clinical trial of 63 patients already taking medication, the treatment proved safe, easy to use at home, and well tolerated.

stories.title: Is your Medicare Advantage plan ending next year? Here's what to know
stories.summary: Medicare open enrollment runs through Dec. 7, and for as many as 5 million seniors, it will be important to log on and pick a new plan.

stories.title: ‘Burden and loss’ builds in DR Congo, as Kenya strengthens Ebola containment
stories.summary: As Ebola continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), more resources are needed to fight the disease and feed patients and families, UN agencies said on Friday.

stories.title: 'Wildly unfair that my husband and I pay £4k a year for ADHD treatment'
stories.summary: Northern Ireland is the only part of the UK without a formally commissioned, publicly-funded adult service for ADHD.

stories.title: Anxiety builds over Medicaid work requirements
stories.summary: As a Boston judge heard a challenge to Medicaid work requirements, state Medicaid directors gathered in Maryland to figure out how to implement those sweeping changes.

stories.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
stories.summary: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.

stories.title: India slashes cost of cancer drugs after court rules mark-ups are ‘extortion’
stories.summary: Case filed in 2022 by patient unable to afford medicine leads to cap on drug prices for millions who face ruin if diagnosed The Indian government has moved to reduce the price of cancer drugs after a retired bank clerk took her case to the supreme court.

stories.title: María Neira: Planetary Health Pioneer, Geneva Veteran, Civil Society Candidate – And a Realist in a Changing Climate?
stories.summary: Who will steer the World Health Organization through its next chapter? Explore Health Policy Watch’s daily series examining the platforms, records, and institutional hurdles facing each contender for WHO Director-General, continuing today with Dr María Neira.

stories.title: Opinion: New Medicare policies will keep important pain relief from some patients
stories.summary: For some people, simply putting on pants can be excruciatingly painful. New policy will put pain relief out of reach for many, doctor writes.

stories.title: Will a macaque eat a grape sitting on a pile of poo? A study on germophobia
stories.summary: When an outbreak strikes, humans try to avoid germs. (Remember wiping off groceries at the start of the pandemic?) What about ... monkeys?

stories.title: A GOP congressman voted to cut Medicaid. It covers 62% of his district. Can he win?
stories.summary: Republican U.S. Rep. David Valadao is fighting for reelection in central California. 6 in 10 residents of his district are covered by Medicaid, which he voted to cut last year.

stories.title: Abu Dhabi Wants Health Systems to See Disease Coming. But Who Owns the Data and Who Gets Left Out?
stories.summary: At the Abu Dhabi Future Health Summit, ministers and officials from Greece to Jordan lined up to learn from the emirate’s bet on genomes, wearables and artificial intelligence.

stories.title: Big pharma accused of ‘free-riding on nature’ as global fund attracts just $7,000
stories.summary: The Cali Fund, set up to raise $1bn a year for biodiversity from drug companies, remains near empty Big pharmaceutical companies have been accused of “free-riding on nature”, after a landmark biodiversity fund that invites businesses to put some of their profits back into conservation was left...

stories.title: Did Nigeria and Kenya’s Ebola Patients Cross Paths in Uganda Airport?
stories.summary: Nigeria’s first Ebola Bundibugyo patient may have crossed paths with Kenya’s recently deceased index patient at Uganda’s Entebbe Airport on 3 October, according to Dr Wessam Mankoula, head of health emergencies at Africa Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC).

stories.title: DR Congo: Ebola responders under pressure as outbreak expands
stories.summary: As the deadly Ebola disease outbreak reached an eighth province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), investigators pursued all leads on Thursday to assess the risk of the disease spreading in Nigeria.

stories.title: First human case of Shamonda virus detected in France, officials say
stories.summary: The disease, which usually affects cattle, has been identified in a patient who died in early October.

stories.title: First human case of Shamonda virus reported in France as patient dies
stories.summary: A patient in France has died after being infected with Shamonda virus, the first recorded human case of the disease.

stories.title: Give more people weight loss jabs on the NHS, say MPs
stories.summary: Current plans for 6% of eligible patients to get Mounjaro by 2028 unambitious, say MPs.

stories.title: Haematology centre for cancer patients at risk over 'disgraceful' funds move
stories.summary: The Department of Health has decided to take back £1.5m from the project, Belfast Trust officials have told a Stormont committee.

stories.title: Health insurance premiums jump 9%, and more Americans don’t have access to coverage
stories.summary: Working-age U.S. adults without health insurance rose in 2026. Half of all uninsured people did not seek needed care because of cost concerns, according to a new survey.

stories.title: High health costs squeeze workers, even if you have good insurance through a job
stories.summary: About 157 million Americans get their health insurance through work. A survey of employers shows a moderate price uptick this year, but workers still say health costs are a top concern.

stories.title: MI5 spied on NHS founder Nye Bevan for more than 20 years, newly released files show
stories.summary: He came to its attention in the 1930s when he was considered a left-wing firebrand.

stories.title: Private care home investors a risk to public sector, regulator says
stories.summary: US investors are buying up UK care homes - a situation regulators say they are "watching carefully" in case it threatens plans for a National Care Service.

stories.title: Chronic UTIs affect millions in the UK - these women are out to end the stigma
stories.summary: Women are sharing their experiences with chronic urinary tract infections on social media in an effort to break the stigma surrounding UTIs.

stories.title: Diabetes and ADHD drugs to be tested on Alzheimer's patients in new study
stories.summary: Drugs will be tested simultaneously, which it's hoped will speed up the process of finding new treatments for this common type of dementia.

stories.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
stories.summary: Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.

stories.title: Nigeria identifies travel-related Ebola case

stories.title: Opinion: How knocking on doors can help beat measles ,  again
stories.summary: “As measles outbreaks spread in the U.S., it may be time to learn how other countries get their outbreaks under control,” writes Raj Panjabi.

stories.title: Opinion: Replication is necessary even if scientists do everything right
stories.summary: “Committing a Type 1 error does not reflect poorly on the quality of the science done,” writes Mark Louie F. Ramos
